questions.stem: 'Gadgil Committee Report' and 'Kasturirangan Committee Report', sometimes seen in the news, are related to
questions.explanation_md:
**Both reports are on conserving the Western Ghats.**

- **Gadgil Committee (Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel, 2011)** — chaired by **Madhav Gadgil**; recommended declaring the **entire Western Ghats an Ecologically Sensitive Area**, graded into ESZ I, II, III, with a Western Ghats Ecology Authority. States called it anti-development.
- **Kasturirangan Committee (High Level Working Group, 2013)** — chaired by **K. Kasturirangan**; diluted this, marking only about **37% of the Ghats (≈60,000 sq km) as ecologically sensitive**, splitting the region into cultural and natural landscapes and banning mining, quarrying and red-category industry only in the ESA.
- The Ghats run through six states — Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu — and are a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and one of the world's biodiversity hotspots.
questions.tagging_note: Western Ghats as a biodiversity hotspot (ENV-05) plus the Ecologically Sensitive Area notification under the EPA (ENV-09). No topic in the vocabulary covers named expert-committee reports as such — this is a genuine gap for the recurring 'committee report in the news' question type.

questions.stem:
Consider the following :
1. Calcutta Unitarian Committee
2. Tabernacle of New Dispensation
3. Indian Reform Association
Keshab Chandra Sen is associated with the establishment of which of the above?
questions.explanation_md:
**Keshab Chandra Sen founded the Indian Reform Association (1870) and the Nava Vidhan / Church of the New Dispensation (1880); the Calcutta Unitarian Committee was Rammohan Roy's.**

- **Statement 1 — wrong.** The **Calcutta Unitarian Committee (1821)** was set up by **Raja Rammohan Roy** with William Adam and Dwarkanath Tagore — years before Keshab was born (1838).
- **Statement 2 — correct.** After splitting from the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj group, Keshab proclaimed the **Nava Vidhan, "Tabernacle of the New Dispensation" (1880)**, a syncretic faith drawing on all religions.
- **Statement 3 — correct.** He founded the **Indian Reform Association (1870)** on returning from England — working on cheap literature, female education, temperance and charity; it fed into the **Native Marriage Act (Civil Marriage Act), 1872**.
- Keshab's other landmark: the **Brahmo Samaj of India (1866)**, formed after breaking with Debendranath Tagore.

2 and 3 → **(b)**.
questions.tagging_note: Keshab Chandra Sen and the Brahmo splinter organisations sit in HIS-05; HIS-16 covers the personalities appendix.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** a member of 'Gulf Cooperation Council'?
questions.explanation_md:
**Iran is not in the GCC — the GCC is the six Arab monarchies of the Persian Gulf.**

- Members (founded **1981, Abu Dhabi**): **Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman**. Mnemonic: **S-U-K-Q-B-O**.
- Iran is excluded by design — the Council was formed largely as an Arab, Sunni-monarchy counterweight after the **1979 Iranian Revolution** and at the start of the Iran–Iraq war. **Iraq and Yemen are also not members.**
- Headquarters: **Riyadh**. Its joint military arm is the **Peninsula Shield Force**.
questions.tagging_note: GCC is not named in CAI-05 (which lists SAARC, BIMSTEC, IORA, ASEAN) but regional groupings is the correct bucket; CAI-03 covers West Asia. The topic name under-enumerates the groupings UPSC actually asks about.
questions.transcription_note: 'not' is printed in bold italic in the source; retained as markdown emphasis.

questions.stem:
What is/are the purpose/purposes of Government's 'Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme' and 'Gold Monetization Scheme'?
1. To bring the idle gold lying with Indian households into the economy
2. To promote FDI in the gold and jewellery sector
3. To reduce India's dependence on gold imports
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**Both schemes exist to mobilise idle household gold and thereby cut gold imports — neither has anything to do with FDI.**

- **1 — correct.** Gold Monetization Scheme (2015) lets households/temples deposit physical gold with banks and earn interest; SGB gives a paper substitute so people stop buying physical gold. Both pull idle gold into the formal economy.
- **2 — wrong.** FDI in gold/jewellery is a separate policy matter (100% under automatic route already). Neither scheme touches it. This statement is the classic distractor.
- **3 — correct.** Gold imports are the second-largest item in India's import bill and a key driver of the CAD. Recycling domestic gold and substituting bonds for bars reduces import demand.

Answer: **1 and 3 only**.
questions.tagging_note: Straddles instrument design (SGB is a G-Sec-linked bond, GMS a bank deposit product — Pillar 1D) and the external sector rationale (statement 3 is about cutting gold imports and the CAD, ECO-12). No topic in the vocabulary names gold schemes or the gold import/CAD problem explicitly; ECO-08 is the closest home for the instruments themselves.

questions.stem: 'Belt and Road Initiative' is sometimes mentioned in the news in the context of the affairs of
questions.explanation_md:
**Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is China's connectivity project, announced by Xi Jinping in 2013.**

Two components: the land-based **Silk Road Economic Belt** (Central Asia–Europe) and the **21st Century Maritime Silk Road** (South China Sea–Indian Ocean–Africa). Earlier called OBOR (One Belt One Road).

India has stayed out, chiefly because **CPEC** — a BRI flagship — runs through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, violating India's sovereignty.
questions.tagging_note: BRI is China's connectivity programme, so it sits under the China portion of CAI-01, but the vocabulary is India-centric and CAI-06 ('connectivity projects') is written for India's own economic diplomacy. Neither topic names BRI/CPEC directly.

questions.stem: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana is aimed at
options: bringing the small entrepreneurs into formal financial system
providing loans to poor farmers for cultivating particular crops
providing pensions to old and destitute persons
funding the voluntary organizations involved in the promotion of skill development and employment generation
questions.explanation_md:
**MUDRA = Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency**, launched 8 April 2015. It refinances lenders who give collateral-free loans up to ₹10 lakh to non-farm, non-corporate micro enterprises — i.e. **it pulls small entrepreneurs into the formal financial system**.

Three categories (memorise these):
- **Shishu** — up to ₹50,000
- **Kishore** — ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh
- **Tarun** — ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh

Not farm credit (b), not a pension (that's Atal Pension Yojana, c), not NGO/skill funding (d).

questions.stem:
In which of the following regions of India are shale gas resources found?
1. Cambay Basin
2. Cauvery Basin
3. Krishna-Godavari Basin
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**All three basins have shale gas potential.** India's shale prospectivity was assessed across six sedimentary basins: **Cambay, Cauvery, Krishna-Godavari, Assam-Arakan, Gondwana and Indo-Gangetic**.

The first shale gas exploratory well was drilled by ONGC at **Jambusar in the Cambay basin (Gujarat), 2013**.

When a UPSC question lists three of India's well-known petroliferous basins and asks about shale, **the safe reading is "all of them"** — these are exactly the Category-I basins with proven commercial hydrocarbons and organic-rich shales.

Answer: **1, 2 and 3**.

questions.stem: 'Global Financial Stability Report' is prepared by the
options: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
questions.explanation_md:
**The Global Financial Stability Report (GFSR) is an IMF publication** — twice yearly (April and October), assessing risks to the global financial system.

Keep the IMF's other flagships straight:
- **World Economic Outlook (WEO)** — growth projections
- **Fiscal Monitor** — public finances
- **Global Financial Stability Report** — financial-sector risk

World Bank publishes *Global Economic Prospects*, *World Development Report*, *Ease of Doing Business*.

questions.stem:
Regarding 'Atal Pension Yojana', which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is a minimum guaranteed pension scheme mainly targeted at unorganized sector workers.
2. Only one member of a family can join the scheme.
3. Same amount of pension is guaranteed for the spouse for life after subscriber's death.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**Statement 2 is the killer — APY has no one-per-family restriction.**

- **1 — correct.** APY (June 2015, run by PFRDA) guarantees ₹1,000–₹5,000 monthly pension from age 60, explicitly aimed at **unorganised sector workers**.
- **2 — wrong.** Any eligible individual with a bank account can join; several members of one family may each subscribe. (The one-member-per-family cap belongs to schemes like Ujjwala/PMJDY-type targeting, not APY.)
- **3 — correct.** On the subscriber's death the **spouse receives the same guaranteed pension for life**, and after the spouse's death the accumulated corpus goes to the nominee.

Answer: **1 and 3 only**.
questions.tagging_note: APY is a PFRDA-run guaranteed pension scheme for unorganised workers. The vocabulary has no topic for the pension/insurance sector (PFRDA, NPS, PMJJBY/PMSBY) — a genuine gap. Tagged to financial inclusion (ECO-06), with the social-security-scheme angle under ECO-17 and the scheme-facts angle under CAI-10.

questions.stem: The term 'Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership' often appears in the news in the context of the affairs of a group of countries known as
questions.explanation_md:
**RCEP is ASEAN-centred** — negotiations launched at the ASEAN Summit in Phnom Penh, 2012.

Composition: the **10 ASEAN members + their 6 FTA partners** (China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and India). **India walked out in November 2019** over the trade deficit with China, inadequate safeguards, and the base-year issue; the remaining 15 signed in 2020.

Not G20, not SCO, not SAARC.

questions.stem:
On which of the following can you find the Bureau of Energy Efficiency Star Label?
1. Ceiling fans
2. Electric geysers
3. Tubular fluorescent lamps
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**All three carry the BEE Star Label.** BEE (set up under the **Energy Conservation Act, 2001**) runs the Standards & Labelling programme, started 2006.

By 2016 the **mandatory** list included frost-free refrigerators, room ACs, **tubular fluorescent lamps (TFLs)**, distribution transformers, room ACs, colour TVs, **electric geysers/storage water heaters** and **ceiling fans**.

The 1–5 star scale: **more stars = less energy consumed**.

Answer: **1, 2 and 3**.
questions.tagging_note: Real gap: no topic covers energy efficiency, the Bureau of Energy Efficiency, the Energy Conservation Act or star labelling. ENV-16 is the nearest ('national missions', e.g. NMEEE) and ECO-16 covers energy in the infrastructure sense, but neither genuinely contains this content. Worth adding an energy-efficiency line to ENV-16's scope.

questions.stem: India is an important member of the 'International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor'. If this experiment succeeds, what is the immediate advantage for India?
options: It can use thorium in place of uranium for power generation
It can attain a global role in satellite navigation
It can drastically improve the efficiency of its fission reactors in power generation
It can build fusion reactors for power generation
questions.explanation_md:
**ITER is a fusion experiment — so the direct payoff is the ability to build fusion reactors.**

ITER (Cadarache, France) is a tokamak using **deuterium–tritium fusion** with magnetic confinement. Members: India, EU, USA, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea. India joined in 2005; the domestic agency is **ITER-India (IPR, Gandhinagar)**.

Why the others fail:
- (a) Thorium belongs to the **three-stage fission programme** (AHWR), not fusion.
- (b) Satellite navigation is NAVIC/ISRO — unrelated.
- (c) ITER is fusion, so it cannot improve **fission** reactor efficiency.

Read the question's own words: *Thermonuclear* = fusion.

questions.stem:
In the context of the history of India, consider the following pairs :

| | *Term* | *Description* |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Eripatti | Land, revenue from which was set apart for the maintenance of the village tank |
| 2. | Taniyurs | Villages donated to a single Brahmin or a group of Brahmins |
| 3. | Ghatikas | Colleges generally attached to the temples |

Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation_md:
**Chola-era village administration terms — pair 2 is the wrong one.**

- **1 — correct.** *Eripatti* ("tank land") — revenue from this land was reserved for **maintenance of the village tank**, crucial in the dry Tamil country.
- **2 — WRONG.** *Taniyur* was a **large village that had grown big enough to be a revenue unit / taluk on its own**, separated from its earlier *kurram*. The description given — a village gifted to Brahmins — is **Brahmadeya** (or *Agrahara*; *Devadana* was land gifted to a temple).
- **3 — correct.** *Ghatikas* were **centres of learning/colleges attached to temples** (e.g. the famous ghatika at Kanchipuram).

Answer: **1 and 3**.
questions.tagging_note: Eripatti and taniyur are Chola village/land-revenue terms (ANM-09); ghatikas are Pallava-era temple colleges, so ANM-08 carries part of it. Format is term-description pairs asking which are correctly matched — 'pairs' is the closest available format even though the options are combinations rather than a count.
questions.transcription_note: The pairs are printed as a two-column Term : Description list under italic headings 'Term' and 'Description'; rendered here as a markdown table.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. The International Solar Alliance was launched at the United Nations Climate Change Conference in 2015.
2. The Alliance includes all the member countries of the United Nations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_md:
**Statement 1 — correct.** The International Solar Alliance (ISA) was launched by PM Modi and President Hollande on **30 November 2015 at COP21 in Paris**, the UN Climate Change Conference. Headquarters: Gurugram (Gwal Pahari), India — the first international body headquartered in India.

**Statement 2 — wrong.** At launch, ISA membership was open **only to countries lying fully or partly between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn** (the "sunshine belt", ~121 prospective countries). It was *not* all UN members. (The framework agreement was only amended in 2020 to open membership to all UN members — after this exam.)

So **1 only** → (a).
questions.tagging_note: Straddles Environment and IR. Statement 1 is about the COP21 launch (climate governance, ENV-13); statement 2 is about membership of a treaty-based international grouping (CAI-04). ENV-16 covers the solar/renewables mission angle. No topic in the vocabulary names the ISA specifically.

questions.stem: 'European Stability Mechanism', sometimes seen in the news, is an
options: agency created by EU to deal with the impact of millions of refugees arriving from Middle East
agency of EU that provides financial assistance to eurozone countries
agency of EU to deal with all the bilateral and multilateral agreements on trade
agency of EU to deal with the conflicts arising among the member countries
questions.explanation_md:
The **European Stability Mechanism (ESM)** is the eurozone's permanent **bailout fund**, based in Luxembourg, operational since October 2012. It replaced the temporary EFSF/EFSM.

**It raises money on capital markets and lends to eurozone member states in financial distress** (Greece, Cyprus, Spain's banks) against agreed reform conditionality.

Key discriminator: it is about **financial assistance to eurozone countries**, not refugees (that's EASO/relocation schemes), not trade, not dispute settlement (that's the CJEU). → (b).
questions.tagging_note: Gap: the vocabulary has no topic on EU/eurozone institutions or regional financial-stability mechanisms. ECO-13 (IMF, World Bank, WTO, ADB, NDB) is the closest home for an international financial institution; CAI-07 catches the global-governance framing.

questions.stem:
Which of the following is/are the advantage/advantages of practising drip irrigation?
1. Reduction in weed
2. Reduction in soil salinity
3. Reduction in soil erosion
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
options: None of the above is an advantage of practising drip irrigation
questions.explanation_md:
**1. Reduction in weed — correct.** Drip delivers water **only at the root zone of the crop**; the inter-row soil stays dry, so weed seeds don't germinate. Weed growth falls sharply vs flood irrigation.

**2. Reduction in soil salinity — wrong.** Drip does *not* reduce salinity. Because there is no excess water percolating down, **salts are not leached away — they accumulate at the wetting front / periphery of the wetted zone**. Drip *manages* salinity by keeping salts away from roots, but salt build-up in the soil actually increases; periodic leaching is still needed.

**3. Reduction in soil erosion — correct.** No flowing sheet of water across the field, low discharge at each emitter, no runoff → negligible erosion.

**1 and 3 only** → (c).

questions.stem:
Regarding 'DigiLocker', sometimes seen in the news, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is a digital locker system offered by the Government under Digital India Programme.
2. It allows you to access your e-documents irrespective of your physical location.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**Statement 1 — correct.** DigiLocker is a **flagship initiative of MeitY under the Digital India programme**, launched 2015. Linked to Aadhaar; provides cloud storage plus issuer-pushed documents (driving licence, RC, CBSE marksheets, PAN).

**Statement 2 — correct.** It is **cloud-based**, so documents are accessible from any device, anywhere — that is the whole point of a "digital locker".

IT (Amendment) Rules 2016 gave DigiLocker documents **legal parity with original physical documents**.

**Both 1 and 2** → (c).
questions.tagging_note: DigiLocker sits under e-governance (POL-27); also a trackable Digital India scheme (CAI-10).

questions.stem: Recently, linking of which of the following rivers was undertaken?
questions.explanation_md:
The **Godavari–Krishna link** — the **Pattiseema Lift Irrigation Scheme** in Andhra Pradesh — was commissioned in **September 2015**, lifting Godavari water into the Polavaram Right Main Canal to feed the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage.

It was publicised as **India's first river-interlinking project actually completed on the ground**, making Godavari–Krishna the answer for "recently undertaken".

The others: Ken–Betwa was the first *approved* NPP link (not completed); Mahanadi–Godavari is a proposed peninsular link; Narmada–Tapti and Cauvery–Tungabhadra were not undertaken. → (b).

questions.stem:
In the cities of our country, which among the following atmospheric gases are normally considered in calculating the value of Air Quality Index?
1. Carbon dioxide
2. Carbon monoxide
3. Nitrogen dioxide
4. Sulfur dioxide
5. Methane
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
India's **National Air Quality Index (launched April 2015, "One Number – One Colour – One Description")** monitors **eight pollutants**: PM10, PM2.5, **NO₂, SO₂, CO**, O₃, NH₃ and Pb.

**Carbon dioxide (1) and methane (5) are NOT in the AQI** — they are greenhouse gases, not criteria air pollutants harmful at ambient concentrations to human health.

So from the list: **2 (CO), 3 (NO₂), 4 (SO₂)** → (b).

AQI bands: Good 0–50, Satisfactory 51–100, Moderate 101–200, Poor 201–300, Very Poor 301–400, Severe 401–500.

questions.stem:
With reference to 'Astrosat', the astronomical observatory launched by India, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Other than USA and Russia, India is the only country to have launched a similar observatory into space.
2. Astrosat is a 2000 kg satellite placed in an orbit at 1650 km above the surface of the Earth.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**Statement 1 — wrong.** India is not the only country besides USA and Russia with a space observatory. **Japan (ASCA, Suzaku, Hitomi), the ESA (XMM-Newton, Herschel) and others have launched space observatories.** Astrosat's real distinction is being India's **first dedicated multi-wavelength observatory**, observing simultaneously in UV, optical and X-ray (soft and hard).

**Statement 2 — wrong on both numbers.** Astrosat (launched 28 Sept 2015 by PSLV-C30) weighs about **1513 kg** and was placed in a near-equatorial orbit at about **650 km**, inclination 6° — not 2000 kg at 1650 km.

**Neither 1 nor 2** → (d).

questions.stem: With reference to the economic history of medieval India, the term 'Araghatta' refers to
options: land grants made to military officers
waterwheel used in the irrigation of land
questions.explanation_md:
**'Araghatta'** = **arahatta / rahat**, the **Persian wheel — a waterwheel used to lift water from a well for irrigation**.

Etymology gives it away: *ara* (spoke of a wheel) + *ghatta* (pot) — **a wheel fitted with pots**, the classic chain-of-pots lift device. It appears in medieval texts and inscriptions as a mark of improved irrigation technology.

Distractors: bonded labour = *vishti*/*begar*; land grants to officers = *iqta*/*jagir*. → (c).
questions.tagging_note: Gap: no topic covers medieval economic history or agricultural technology as such. ANM-11 is the only topic whose scope includes 'Delhi Sultanate — administration, economy'; ANM-10 covers the early-medieval period in which the Araghatta (Persian wheel precursor) is usually placed.

questions.stem: With reference to the cultural history of India, the memorizing of chronicles, dynastic histories and epic tales was the profession of who of the following?
questions.explanation_md:
**Maagadha (Magadha)** — the **bards/genealogists who memorised and recited dynastic genealogies, chronicles and epic tales**, mentioned alongside *suta* and *vandin* as court panegyrists. The *suta–magadha* pair is the standard term for the reciters who preserved the *itihasa-purana* tradition orally.

Distractors:
- **Shramana** — wandering ascetic of the heterodox (Buddhist/Jain/Ajivika) traditions.
- **Parivrajaka** — wandering mendicant/renunciant.
- **Agrahaarika** — recipient/holder of an *agrahara*, a tax-free land grant to Brahmanas.

→ (d).
questions.tagging_note: Real gap: no topic covers ancient Indian social categories and professions (Shramana, Parivrajaka, Agrahaarika, Maagadha). ART-10 (literature, languages, philosophy) is the nearest fit via the oral bardic/epic tradition; ANM-04 covers the Shramana/Parivrajaka ascetic terms and ANM-02 the Vedic-era suta/magadha bards. None of the three genuinely owns this question.

questions.stem: Recently, for the first time in our country, which of the following States has declared a particular butterfly as 'State Butterfly'?
questions.explanation_md:
**Maharashtra**, in **June 2015**, became the **first Indian State to declare a State Butterfly — the Blue Mormon (*Papilio polymnestor*)**.

It is India's **second-largest butterfly** (after the Southern Birdwing), found in the Western Ghats, Sri Lanka and coastal Maharashtra.

Later states followed (Uttarakhand — Common Peacock, Karnataka — Southern Birdwing), but the question asks who did it **first**. → (d).

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
The Mangalyaan launched by ISRO
1. is also called the Mars Orbiter Mission
2. made India the second country to have a spacecraft orbit the Mars after USA
3. made India the only country to be successful in making its spacecraft orbit the Mars in its very first attempt
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_md:
**India was the 4th entity to orbit Mars, not the 2nd — that kills statement 2.**

- **1 — Correct.** Mangalyaan *is* the Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM), launched 5 Nov 2013 by PSLV-C25, inserted into Mars orbit 24 Sep 2014.
- **2 — Wrong.** The USSR, USA (NASA) and the European Space Agency had all orbited Mars before India. India was fourth, and first *Asian* nation.
- **3 — Correct.** No country had succeeded on its maiden Mars attempt before India; the USSR, USA, ESA, Japan and China all failed at least once first.

So 1 and 3 only.

questions.stem: What was the main reason for the split in the Indian National Congress at Surat in 1907?
options: Introduction of communalism into Indian politics by Lord Minto
Extremists' lack of faith in the capacity of the moderates to negotiate with the British Government
Aurobindo Ghosh's inability to be elected as the President of the Indian National Congress
questions.explanation_md:
**Surat 1907 was a Moderate–Extremist quarrel, not a communal one.**

Tilak, Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal wanted the 1906 Calcutta resolutions (swaraj, swadeshi, boycott, national education) carried forward and had **no faith that the Moderates' "prayer and petition" method could extract anything from the British**. The Moderates pushed Rash Behari Ghosh as president; the session broke up in disorder and the Congress split until the **Lucknow Pact, 1916**.

- (a) Minto's communal electorates came via the **Morley-Minto Reforms 1909**, after Surat.
- (c) Muslim League was founded Dec 1906 — separate development, not the cause.
- (d) Aurobindo was never a candidate for president.

questions.stem:
Consider the following pairs :

| | *Famous place* | | *Region* |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | Bodhgaya | : | Baghelkhand |
| 2. | Khajuraho | : | Bundelkhand |
| 3. | Shirdi | : | Vidarbha |
| 4. | Nasik (Nashik) | : | Malwa |
| 5. | Tirupati | : | Rayalaseema |

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation_md:
**Only Khajuraho–Bundelkhand and Tirupati–Rayalaseema hold.**

- **1 Bodhgaya : Baghelkhand — wrong.** Bodhgaya is in **Bihar (Magadh region)**. Baghelkhand is the Rewa–Satna belt of eastern MP.
- **2 Khajuraho : Bundelkhand — correct.** Chhatarpur district, MP, in Bundelkhand.
- **3 Shirdi : Vidarbha — wrong.** Shirdi is in **Ahmadnagar district, western Maharashtra (Desh)**; Vidarbha is Nagpur–Amravati, eastern Maharashtra.
- **4 Nasik : Malwa — wrong.** Nashik is **north Maharashtra**, on the Godavari. Malwa is the Indore–Ujjain plateau of MP.
- **5 Tirupati : Rayalaseema — correct.** Chittoor district, one of the four Rayalaseema districts (with Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur).

Only (c) contains just 2 and 5.
questions.tagging_note: Pure location/atlas recall of Indian cultural-physiographic regions (Baghelkhand, Bundelkhand, Vidarbha, Malwa, Rayalaseema). GEO-24 map work is the drill that fixes this; GEO-12 (India physiography) is where the regional divisions are read. The vocabulary has no dedicated 'regions of India' topic, so this is split across the two.

questions.stem: Recently, which of the following States has explored the possibility of constructing an artificial inland port to be connected to sea by a long navigational channel?
questions.explanation_md:
**Rajasthan — a landlocked state exploring a man-made inland port.**

The proposal was for a port in western Rajasthan (the Barmer–Jalore side) linked to the **Arabian Sea through a long navigational channel cut across the Rann of Kutch/Gujarat coast**, to save the state's crude, lignite and mineral traffic the long haul to Kandla/Mundra.

Elimination is the safer route here: **Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka already have sea coast and real ports**, so an "artificial inland port connected to the sea by a long channel" makes no sense for them. That leaves the two landlocked options, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan — and only Rajasthan sits near enough to a coast (the Rann) for a navigational channel to be conceivable.
questions.tagging_note: A 2016 places-in-news item (artificial inland port with a navigational channel to the sea). Nearest genuine fits are ports/inland waterways under GEO-20 transport and infrastructure under ECO-16, but the vocabulary has no static topic that actually carries this specific news item — it would have been picked up only via current affairs.

questions.stem:
With reference to the Agreement at the UNFCCC Meeting in Paris in 2015, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The Agreement was signed by all the member countries of the UN and it will go into effect in 2017.
2. The Agreement aims to limit the greenhouse gas emissions so that the rise in average global temperature by the end of this century does not exceed 2 °C or even 1·5 °C above pre-industrial levels.
3. Developed countries acknowledged their historical responsibility in global warming and committed to donate $ 1000 billion a year from 2020 to help developing countries to cope with climate change.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation_md:
**Only the temperature-goal statement is right.**

- **1 — Wrong** on both counts. The Paris Agreement was adopted by the **195 parties to the UNFCCC**, not "all member countries of the UN", and it **entered into force on 4 November 2016**, not 2017.
- **2 — Correct.** Article 2: hold the rise in global average temperature to **well below 2 °C above pre-industrial levels**, pursuing efforts to limit it to **1.5 °C**.
- **3 — Wrong on the figure.** The finance pledge is **$100 billion a year from 2020** (a floor, to be revised upward before 2025), not $1000 billion. The Agreement also uses "common but differentiated responsibilities", not an explicit admission of historical guilt.

So 2 only.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. The Sustainable Development Goals were first proposed in 1972 by a global think tank called the 'Club of Rome'.
2. The Sustainable Development Goals have to be achieved by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_md:
**The Club of Rome gave the world *Limits to Growth* (1972) — not the SDGs.**

- **1 — Wrong.** The SDG idea came out of the **Rio+20 Conference, 2012**, was drafted by an Open Working Group, and was adopted as the **2030 Agenda by the UN General Assembly in September 2015**, succeeding the MDGs (2000–2015). The Club of Rome's 1972 report is associated with the *limits to growth* thesis, and 1972 is also Stockholm Conference year — both are distractors.
- **2 — Correct.** **17 Goals, 169 targets, deadline 2030.**

So 2 only.
questions.tagging_note: SDG deadline is core ENV-15; the Club of Rome / Limits to Growth distractor also sits in the sustainable-development history covered there.

questions.stem: A recent movie titled *The Man Who Knew Infinity* is based on the biography of
questions.explanation_md:
***The Man Who Knew Infinity* (2015) is about **Srinivasa Ramanujan**.**

Based on Robert Kanigel's biography; Dev Patel plays Ramanujan and Jeremy Irons plays **G. H. Hardy**, covering Ramanujan's journey from Madras Port Trust clerk to Trinity College, Cambridge, and Fellow of the Royal Society. **National Mathematics Day, 22 December, is his birthday.**

The others: Chandrasekhar (Nobel 1983, stellar limit), S. N. Bose (Bose–Einstein statistics), C. V. Raman (Nobel 1930, Raman effect).
questions.tagging_note: Film-and-personality general knowledge (Ramanujan). CAI-09 (awards, sports, personalities and books) is the closest existing topic, but no topic in the vocabulary genuinely covers films or scientist biographies as static GK — this is a real gap the syllabus tree does not cover.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. The minimum age prescribed for any person to be a member of Panchayat is 25 years.
2. A Panchayat reconstituted after premature dissolution continues only for the remainder period.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_md:
**The age is 21, not 25 — that single number decides the question.**

- **1 — Wrong. Article 243F:** a person is qualified to be a member of a Panchayat if he is qualified for election to the **State Legislature**, *except* that **not being under 21 years is enough** — a deliberate lowering from the 25-year MLA/Lok Sabha threshold.
- **2 — Correct. Article 243E(4):** a Panchayat constituted after a premature dissolution serves **only the remainder of the five-year term** of the dissolved body. And if that remainder is **less than six months, no fresh election need be held at all**.

So 2 only.
